author: cperezz.eth
content:
Hey!

We were having discussing with some folks on `SETCODEFROM` (which has been proposed for H* as the way to migrate to smart accounts & save on duplicated-bytecode costs).

We were discussing that considering PBT will index based on codehash, to avoid code duplication in the trie, we will have a way to index based on it that the protocol will be able to rely on.
Thus, instead of `SETCODEFROM`  getting an account argument, we could jump straight into `SETCODEFROMHASH` as Vitalik suggested and preferred.

But, there's a catch, atm, this can't be done as `SELFDESTRUCT` allowed for some time to leave code in code DBs without any account referencing it. That means, we could have consensus issues. **(TLDR, clients have different views on what code does actually really exist in ethereum).**

The proposal is the following:
• All clients engage in an out-of-protocol common effort to bring all code-DBs to match (notice they don't contribute to the root today, hence, this would be nice no matter what to standarize clients)
• Once this is done, we no longer have any issues related to `SETCODEFROMHASH` done in H* instead of doing `SETCODEFROM` to then, change it again or create yet another opcode that does the same.

<@1465657769297182731> <@1252939266871263294> <@316280621783580673> <@543900561460822016> <@281967554572976128> <@954738828445372416> 


Would appreciate your take on this. Either we can discuss here async, or have a call where I can explain this better.

The goal is simple. Agree prior to ACDE next week what route shall we take. 

My proposal is to be a bit more ambicious and go `SETCODEFROMHASH`. But, prefer to do `SETCODEFROM` than do none of them in H*.

Sappy to asnwer any questions or provide more feedback.

EIP link: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8298

author: lu_pinto
content: hmm this looks cool for massive deployments where the hash is fetched once and reused. I guess agreeing on it, implies everyone having to optimize the code fetching through an index. <@680337202521440470> how do you feel about changing the DB?

author: cperezz.eth
content:
I think you all already do that. 
The key question here is whether we want to commit to "fix/unify" our codeDB databases to no longer contain SELFDESTRUCT dangling code that has no account referencing it.

As of today, full-nodes and snap-sync nodes basically dissagree on the code they have. That would change this. But also means we need to decide how we settle which code is good. And how we make sure someone full-syncinc a node doesn't again end up with dangling code in their DB

author: cperezz.eth
content: The benefit of all of this is that we would be aligned with PBT already indexing by hash. And therefore, we can do SETCODEFROMHASH today already.

author: ben_a_adams
content:
Isn't just self destruct; maybe creates that get reverted have already written etc; there isn't any consensus on the contents of the codeDbs matching or required semantics on being strict with what is in them (as additional data is harmless)

Much like still having leaf or intermediate nodes is harmless (and they build up and need to be pruned)

Does code get removed on a block reorg; how do you know is last ref etc

author: ben_a_adams
content:
SETCODEFROM works because you know that account exists, so its code must exist (accounts point that way); but code doesn't point anywhere so you don't know if its live code

Reorgs are the other issue than SELFDESTRUCT; and also hygiene on reverted txs etc

author: ben_a_adams
content: SETCODEFROM is like a 10min change SETCODEFROMHASH is a huge change also will need a start up db clean up that traces every live hash and deletes non live; archive nodes would have issues due to historic self destructs as they will keep their codehashes live but have to mark them as no avilable past a certain point so will need to add over time refcounting to codedb etc?

author: ben_a_adams
content: And can't force archive nodes to resync; as none one has time for that 😉

author: ben_a_adams
content: Very different scales of implementation and ops work

author: tomaj2
content:
IIUC, SETCODEFROM/SETCODEFROMHASH itself can make an account's code become dangling.
If someone deploys a contract that uses SETCODEFROM, that account's code would stop being referenced from the accounts trie once the opcode changes the account's code (unless referenced from another account, of course)

author: cperezz.eth
content:
A lot of things said. Let me address 1 by 1.

1. In-memory layer tree diffs should take care of any reorg issue. As you already know if the code existed or not via it. And if not, that should def be something that should happen today. Is absurd that clients just leave trash there for no reason or treat it differently.
2. No archive needs to re-sync. The update of the CodeDB can be done while it runs even. is just applying a diff mostly.  You can't query code from an archive that no account references. So I don't see how this is an issue for them. We can compute the diff with any client today and share the entire KV to any client to perform the cleanup while still up.
3. We are trading off off-protocol work for in-protocol one. SETCODEFROM works now, but will be "obsolete" with PBT (will still work ofc, but will just be a worse choice). We have the chance to do it right from start.
4. Unify client behaviour when it comes to store or not code when reverts happen I think is tech debt that should have been cleaned long time ago. Is crazy this is still differing across clients.

author: cperezz.eth
content: Finally, is fine if clients don't have appettite for that. Just want to make clear that this is tech debt we have no matter what. And we can take the chance to address it and do things right from the start.

author: cperezz.eth
content:
Yes this is true. And this makes me think that not even with PBT we will fix this problem. And code in that case will live in the trie. So if we want to keep it clean, we will need refcounting no matter what

That was helpful, thanks! 

I might miss something, but indeed I think that is the simple argument that settles the discussion? Unless we do refcounting for code, we can no longer guarantee dangling code doesn't exist if we introduce SETCODEFROM/SETCODEFROMHASH.
